Perkins's 1908 Prairie School refectory on South Pond, crescent in plan: the two-storey Great Hall (its tall round-headed windows lighting the second-floor ballroom), a square pavilion at each end on the water, and the one-storey arcaded loggias joining them; red brick with limestone trim under green tile hipped roofs with deep eaves. Parts traced from the OSM outline; heights, pitches and openings read from photographs (approximate); the windows glow in the evening (an events venue and restaurant)

the 1927 Georgian brick house (its historic exterior kept in the 1992 renovation): red brick with white-framed windows and stone courses under a hipped slate roof, a four-column portico with a pediment on the mall side; portico side, heights and pitch read from photographs (approximate)
the zoo's 1904 bird house (renovated 1991): brick with round-headed windows under a hipped tile roof and a glazed ridge monitor; heights and pitch read from photographs (approximate)
2004, 29,000 sq ft of habitat (sources): stone-clad walls, the glazed viewing band and roof skylights over a planted roof; heights read from photographs (approximate)

1997, 32,000 sq ft, with a 45 ft covered dome recreating a rain forest (PBC Chicago): brick walls and the glass dome to 45 ft (13.7 m); the dome's radius and the walls' height read from photographs (approximate)

the long African habitat house: stone walls, viewing glass and skylit planted roofs on the OSM outline; heights read from photographs (approximate); the exhibit zones OSM maps inside it (Wings in the Wetlands, Life on the Rocks, Dry Thorn Forest, Life in the Lakes) are rooms of this building, not separate houses, and are dropped
an open-air aviary under stainless mesh on steel posts; height read from photographs (approximate)
the snow monkeys' open-air habitat, its viewing structure under mesh; height read from photographs (approximate)
opened October 2016 after Boulders Beach, South Africa: granite-like rock outcrops round the penguins' pool and its underwater viewing window; rock heights approximate
2004: a timber-and-glass house under a planted roof among the woodland habitats (wolves, beavers, otters); heights read from photographs (approximate)
the zoo's offices at 2001 N Clark: brick with white-framed windows under a hipped slate roof; heights read from photographs (approximate)
the zoo hospital and science centre: brick with a glazed band under a flat roof; heights read from photographs (approximate)
Ross Barney Architects' glass and steel visitor centre at the East Gate on Cannon Drive (the zoo's main entrance); heights read from photographs (approximate)

forty-eight hand-carved endangered animals and two chariots (sources) under a round open pavilion; the pavilion's radius from the OSM roof outline (way 210686222), its heights read from photographs (approximate)

the pool at the heart of the zoo, west of the Lion House: rockwork shores and a haul-out island, the curved underwater viewing gallery on its south side (OSM paving 'Under Water Viewing Area'); the pool's outline is not mapped — centred north of the gallery, its size and shape approximate

Farm-in-the-Zoo (1964, renovated 2002): the red main barn with white trim, a gambrel roof in dark shingle over its two blocks (from the OSM outline), cross-braced doors, a ventilator cupola, and the silo where the outline rounds it; heights and pitches read from photographs (approximate)
the red dairy barn, gambrel-roofed; heights read from photographs (approximate)
a red gable-roofed barn; heights read from photographs (approximate)
a small red gable-roofed barn; heights read from photographs (approximate)
the farm's red gable-roofed house barn; heights read from photographs (approximate)

the zoo's newer pavilions and habitat houses, each on its OSM outline in its material — stone, timber or glass and steel — with glazed viewing bands under planted or membrane roofs; materials and heights read from photographs (approximate)
the zoo's older brick houses (the train station is red brick, per the sources), hipped roofs over their OSM outlines; heights and roofs read from photographs (approximate)

the zoo's unnamed service buildings, keepers' houses and habitat shelters: low stone-clad walls with a viewing band under planted roofs, so none reads as an office block; heights read from photographs (approximate)
a small red farm building at Farm-in-the-Zoo, gable-roofed; heights approximate

Graham, Anderson, Probst & White's 1932 Georgian building, its tall porticoed entrance facing east into the park; the 1972 and 1988 (Holabird & Root) additions refaced in red brick to match, the main entrance now on Clark Street. Red brick with limestone trim and white-framed windows on the OSM outline (three storeys, 15 m to the parapet, approximate); a six-column pedimented portico on the park face (column count read from photographs, approximate); no cupola (none confirmed)

the 1999 museum of the Chicago Academy of Sciences (Perkins & Will): a low angular building of pale stone and glass on the OSM outline, planted roofs, the glass Judy Istock Butterfly Haven (2,700 sq ft) on its south wing and terraces stepping down west toward North Pond; the stone (the sources confirm steel and glass), the haven's place and all heights read from photographs (approximate)

Dwight Perkins's 1912 skaters' warming shelter on North Pond, since 1998 a restaurant in the Arts & Crafts manner: a single-storey brick lodge under a deep hipped roof (the roof form, its pitch and the openings read from photographs, approximate) on the OSM outline (2610 N Cannon Dr)

Dwight Perkins's 1913 Prairie-style Fresh Air Fund sanitarium (built 1920, a theatre since 1953, renovated 2017): brick with sweeping arched openings (the steel arched trusses kept in 2017, sources) under a low hipped roof on the OSM outline; heights, roof and tile colour read from photographs (approximate)

Egerton Swartwout's 1926 memorial: an Indiana limestone rotunda ringed by Ionic columns under Adolph Weinman's frieze, between two low wings round their courtyards; the rotunda's centre and radius from the OSM outline's round bay; the dome's interior rises ~95 ft (sources), its exterior height (35 m to the lantern) and the column count read from photographs (approximate)
Ernst Rau's 1886 bronze (recast by William Pelargus) on a granite base, overlooking the formal garden and the Conservatory; its heights and facing read from photographs (approximate)

Johannes Gelert's 1896 8 ft (2.44 m) bronze: Andersen seated on a tree stump with a book, a swan at his feet, on a granite pedestal; position from a map listing and the pedestal read from photographs (approximate)
Richard Henry Park's 1896 bronze, 9 ft 6 in (2.9 m), on a white granite pedestal (Wikipedia); the pedestal's height and the facing read from photographs (approximate)

John Angel's 13 ft (3.96 m) gilded bronze, re-gilded and returned in 2017 facing north as in 1952, on its red granite block (the 78 ft black stele behind it was demolished in 1993); the pedestal's height read from photographs (approximate)
Gutzon Borglum's 1915 bronze: the governor's hand stretched over a working man, his wife and child; the group's height and its low base read from photographs (approximate)
Cyrus Dallin's 1890 equestrian bronze of a Sioux chief in war bonnet, his spear raised, on a granite base; height and facing read from photographs (approximate)

Tony Hunt's 1986 red cedar pole (40 ft, 12.2 m), carved after the 1929 original: the sea monster at its foot, the man riding the whale, Kwanusila the Thunderbird at the top with his wings spread, painted black, red and blue-green (sources); the carving is suggested by turned figures, the wings' span and the facing approximate

Ralph H. Burke's 1940 welded-steel through-arch footbridge over Lake Shore Drive at North Avenue (NRHP; MoMA 1947): two arch ribs over the drive, hangers, concrete approaches at each end. Centre from Wikipedia; the span (the drive's width in OSM), the rise, the deck height and the dark-green paint read from photographs (approximate)

the range at 141 W Diversey (since 1916): the two-storey hitting-bay canopy along its curved tee line (the OSM roof outline, way 210686995), the tee house, and the tall net poles round the landing area to the north; the nets' line (kept off the turf pitch beside it) and their 18 m height estimated from photographs (approximate)
the Park District's arts centre at 2045 N Lincoln Park West: two storeys of brick with white-framed windows under a hipped roof; its form and heights read from photographs (approximate)
a small brick comfort station by Theater on the Lake, hipped roof; heights approximate
a small brick comfort station at Roscoe, hipped roof; heights approximate
the fieldhouse of the South Field: brick under a hipped tile roof; heights approximate
